unit.title: Connectors & discourse
unit.subtitle: Linking words that make you sound fluent

grammar.title: Glue your ideas together like a native
grammar.intro: The gap between "I know words" and "I sound fluent" is often just connectors — the little words that link ideas: however, therefore, although, besides. Learn a handful and your speech stops sounding like a list and starts sounding like a conversation.

sections.heading: Contrast: sin embargo, en cambio, aunque
sections.body: These signal that something goes against what came before. Sin embargo = however; en cambio = on the other hand; aunque = although:

ex.en: I studied a lot; however, I didn't pass.

ex.es: Yo prefiero el mar; ella, en cambio, la montaña.
ex.en: I prefer the sea; she, on the other hand, the mountains.

sections.heading: Result: por lo tanto, así que, por eso
sections.body: These introduce a consequence — the "so" or "therefore" of your sentence. Por lo tanto is a touch more formal; así que and por eso are everyday:

ex.es: Llueve, así que nos quedamos en casa.
ex.en: It's raining, so we're staying home.

ex.es: No había entradas; por lo tanto, cambiamos de plan.
ex.en: There were no tickets; therefore, we changed plans.

sections.heading: Cause & adding: ya que, además
sections.body: Ya que / puesto que give a reason (since, because). Además adds a point (besides, also). Careful too: pero = but; sino = but rather (after a negative):

ex.en: It's cheap and, besides, very good.
It isn't blue, but rather green.

takeaways: Contrast: sin embargo (however), en cambio (on the other hand), aunque (although).
Result: por lo tanto / así que (so, therefore), por eso (that's why).
Cause: ya que / puesto que (since, because). Add: además (besides).
pero = but; sino = but rather, and only after a negative.
aunque + indicative = a real fact; aunque + subjunctive = a possibility.

mistakes.why: After a negative, 'but rather' is sino, not pero.
For a future possibility, aunque takes the subjunctive: aunque llueva.

mistakes.w: Estudié mucho, sin embargo no aprobé sin pausa.
mistakes.r: Estudié mucho; sin embargo, no aprobé.
mistakes.why: Sin embargo starts a new clause — set it off with a semicolon/comma, don't run it on.

exercises.prompt_en: I studied a lot; however, I didn't pass.
It's raining, so we're staying home.

exercises.no: “Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame” — ya que gives the reason.

exercises.prompt_en: It isn't blue, but rather green.
exercises.hint: 'But rather', used after a negative — not 'pero'.
exercises.no: After a negative, 'but rather' is “sino”: no es azul, sino verde.

exercises.prompt: Match each connector to its meaning.

exercises.tts: Hacía frío; por eso, cerré la ventana.
accepted: hacia frio por eso cerre la ventana
exercises.translation: It was cold; that's why I closed the window.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Hacía frío; por eso, cerré la ventana.”
exercises.no: It was: “Hacía frío; por eso, cerré la ventana.” (It was cold; that's why I closed the window.)

exercises.scenario: Debating weekend plans with a friend 🗓️

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.es: El plan al aire libre suena bien, pero dicen que va a llover.
lines.en: The outdoor plan sounds good, but they say it's going to rain.

options.text: Aunque llueva, podemos ir; y además, llevo paraguas.
Aunque llueve, podemos ir; y sin embargo, llevo paraguas.
Por lo tanto llueva, podemos ir; y ya que, llevo paraguas.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! aunque + subjuntivo (posibilidad) y además para añadir. ¡Muy fluido!
exercises.no: A future possibility takes aunque + subjunctive, and 'besides' is además: “Aunque llueva, podemos ir; y además, llevo paraguas.”

exercises.say: Estaba cansado; sin embargo, salí a correr.
exercises.en: I was tired; however, I went out for a run.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound.
